verdict: W. R. Berkley earned $446M — underwriting stayed strong at a 90.8% combined ratio and investment income rose 9%, but a swing from investment gains a year ago to losses this year pulled profit down from $511M.

kpis.label: Combined ratio
kpis.note: underwriting kept $9.20 of every $100 of premium

segments.name: Net premiums earned
segments.note: Premiums from specialty insurance policies, earned over the coverage period — up 2%, with Insurance segment premiums written up about 5% gross and average rates up about 4% outside workers' compensation.

segments.name: Net investment income
segments.note: Interest and dividends on the money Berkley invests between collecting premiums and paying claims — up 9% as the core portfolio grew 12% and fixed-maturity income rose 10%.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Revenues from non-insurance businesses and insurance service fees, reduced by $18M of net investment losses this quarter (a year ago this line included $79M of investment gains).

opex.name: Other operating costs and expenses
opex.note: Underwriting and running costs as Berkley prints them in one line — commissions, salaries and the cost of operating its 60 specialty businesses.

opex.name: Expenses from non-insurance businesses
opex.note: The cost of running the non-insurance businesses whose revenues sit in Other revenues.

otherDetail: The printed statement goes straight from pre-tax income ($574M) to tax. The -$2M shown here is the profit share attributable to noncontrolling interests, leaving $446M for common stockholders.
oneTimers: Net investment losses of $18M (versus gains of $79M a year ago) are inside GAAP net income but excluded from Berkley's operating income of $457M ($1.17 per diluted share).
Catastrophe losses added 2.7 points to the combined ratio; excluding them, the current accident-year combined ratio was 88.1%.

takeaways.title: Underwriting stayed profitable
takeaways.text: The combined ratio of 90.8% means claims and underwriting expenses took about 91 cents of every premium dollar. Insurance segment pre-tax underwriting income grew 10.6% to $238M.

takeaways.title: Investment income keeps climbing
takeaways.text: Net investment income rose 9% to $384M as the core portfolio grew 12%. Operating income — Berkley's preferred measure, which strips out investment gains and losses — rose to $457M, or $1.17 per share.

takeaways.title: An investment swing cut GAAP profit
takeaways.text: Net income fell to $446M from $511M a year ago almost entirely because investments swung from $79M of gains to $18M of losses — the underlying insurance business improved.

footerNote: For an insurer, claims (loss and loss expenses) play the role of cost of revenue. Berkley does not split out policy acquisition costs — its printed 'Other operating costs and expenses' ($1,010M) holds underwriting and operating costs together, so it is shown whole. Figures are converted from the statements' thousands and rounded to $M; 'Other revenues' ($141M) is the balancing total of non-insurance revenues, service fees and other income, less $18M of net investment losses. Net income of $446M is attributable to common stockholders; consolidated net income before noncontrolling interests was $448M.
